newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM KLAUS'S PARTY RETAINS LEAD IN POLL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM KLAUS'S PARTY RETAINS LEAD IN POLL.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) continues to enjoy a lead in support over its nearest rival, the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD), a survey released on Friday showed.
The early February poll by the private STEM agency said 26.2 percent of respondents said they would vote for ODS if an election were held next week, while the CSSD was second with 21.5 percent.

Governing coalition party the centrist Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) were third with 11.2 percent, followed closely by the hard-line Communists (KSCM), who garnered 10.6 percent, and the third coalition member, Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), at 9.6 percent.
The number of undecided voters was 6.7 percent.

The coalition lost its parliamentary majority in last June's elections, gaining 99 seats in the 200-seat chamber, but remained in power as the Social Democrats ruled out a grand coalition with the two extremist parties.
In the vote, ODS received 29.6 percent, the CSSD 26.44 percent, KSCM 10.33 percent, KDU-CSL 8.08 percent and ODA 6.36 percent.

The far-right Republicans (SPR-RSC), the only other party currently with parliamentary representation, slumped to 5.4 percent, down from 8.01 percent in the election, and just above the five percent minimum needed to gain entrance into the parliament.
Some 70 percent of those polled said they would vote in an election if it were held next week. The next general elections are scheduled for June, 2000.
